panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide of Alha and Udal astride horses on a smoky battlefield, Khajuraho-like temple shikhara faint in the distance, sky split between dawn and dusk
panels.action: Alha stands in the foreground, weathered and intense, hand on sword, while a ghostly second figure like Udal overlaps behind him, as carved inscription stones lie half-buried at their feet amid a hazy battlefield.

dialogue.text: In Bundelkhand, Alha and Udal never die; yet the silent stones of Mahoba insist that Paramardi lived on after Prithviraj’s sack. Between ballad and inscription, whose truth holds the weight of that war?

i18n.hi: बुंदेलखंड में अल्हा‑ऊदल अमर हैं, मगर महोबा की ख़ामोश चट्टानें कहती हैं कि पृथ्वीराज की लूट के बाद परमार्दि जिंदा रहे। क़िस्से और शिलालेख के बीच, किसकी सच्चाई उस जंग का भार उठाती है?

panels.shot: epic bird’s-eye over the clustered temples of Khajuraho and the fort of Mahoba, with routes snaking in from the north-west
panels.action: A wide view shows stone temples rising amid trees, the fort of Mahoba crouched beyond a lake, and tiny processions of traders and soldiers moving along dusty tracks under a hot sun.

dialogue.text: Late twelfth-century Bundelkhand: the Chandela kings rule from Mahoba and leave their mark in stone at Khajuraho. But the age of temple-building is ending; an age of raids and rival kings begins.

i18n.hi: बारहवीं सदी के अंत का बुंदेलखंड: चंदेल राजा महोबा से राज करते हैं, खजुराहो के मंदिरों में अपना नाम गढ़ते हैं। पर मंदिरों का दौर ढल रहा है; अब शुरू है लूट, धावे और टकराते तख्तों का ज़माना।

panels.shot: slow push-in toward the ramparts of Mahoba, with a regal figure in silhouette on the battlements
panels.action: A lone royal figure, representing Paramardi-deva, stands on Mahoba’s battlements, robes stirred by the wind, looking out over clustered roofs and temple spires within the walls.

dialogue.text: Paramardi-deva, last great Chandela, holds Mahoba and Kalinjar. To the north-west, the Chauhan ruler Prithviraj III of Ajmer and Delhi watches these lands with a restless, testing gaze.

i18n.hi: परमार्दि‑देव, अंतिम बड़े चंदेल, महोबा और कालिंजर थामे हैं। उत्तर‑पश्चिम में अजमेर‑दिल्ली का चौहान राजा पृथ्वीराज तृतीय इन इलाक़ों पर बेचैन, परखती नज़र टिकाए है।

panels.shot: medium close-up of a bard in a village courtyard at dusk, surrounded by listeners, as he raises his hand dramatically
panels.action: An elderly bard, eyes bright, sits cross-legged in a courtyard, arm lifted mid-gesture as villagers lean in close, lantern light flickering over their faces and the darkening sky behind.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, in village courtyards, a different Mahoba lives. Here, the Alha-Khand and Parmal Raso breathe, telling of fierce generals Alha and Udal under King Parmal’s banner.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद, गाँव की चौपालों में एक और महोबा बसता है। यहाँ अल्हा‑खण्ड और परमार रासो साँस लेते हैं, राजा परमार के परचम तले सेनानियों अल्हा‑ऊदल के धाँसू कारनामे सुनाते हैं।

panels.shot: low, intimate angle on young Alha and Udal side by side, imagined in bardic style, framed by flickering firelight
panels.action: Two warrior brothers, Alha in the foreground with a stern, rugged face, Udal just behind with a hot, eager gaze, stand shoulder to shoulder in stylised armour as sparks from a fire swirl around them.

dialogue.text: In these songs, Alha and Udal are not minor captains. They are the burning heart of Mahoba, foster-sons of King Parmal, whose loyalty and rage shape every turn of the war.

i18n.hi: इन गीतों में अल्हा‑ऊदल मामूली सूबेदार नहीं। वे महोबा की जलती धड़कन हैं, राजा परमार के पालित बेटे, जिनकी वफ़ादारी और गुस्सा हर मोड़ पर जंग की दिशा मोड़ देता है।

panels.shot: dynamic tracking shot along a line of cavalry thundering across dry plains, dust rising, banners whipping
panels.action: A column of horsemen in bardic Chauhan style charges across a parched plain; one turbaned leader evokes Prithviraj, while in the hazy distance a fortified Mahoba stands braced behind its walls.

dialogue.text: The ballads thunder: Prithviraj rides against Mahoba. The brothers swear to hold the Chandela frontier, while proud Rajput houses weigh honour, insult and survival with every step of their horses.

i18n.hi: किस्से गरजते हैं: पृथ्वीराज महोबा पर चढ़ आया। दोनों भाई क़सम खाते हैं कि चंदेल सरहद थामे रखेंगे, जबकि शान‑ओ‑शौकत वाले राजपूत घराने हर क़दम पर इज़्ज़त, अपमान और बचाव तौलते चलते हैं।

panels.shot: chaotic mid-shot of clashing infantry before Mahoba’s walls, with Alha in the foreground crossing swords with a nameless foe
panels.action: Alha, teeth set and eyes fierce, meets an oncoming warrior’s blade just outside Mahoba’s gate; behind them, mixed ranks of warriors crash together under swirling dust and a darkening sky.

dialogue.text: Here the songs give detail where stone is silent. They name duels, betrayals, shifting allies, and a chain of single combats that turn the tide. But on these, the historian walks carefully.

i18n.hi: यहीं गीत बारीकियाँ बताते हैं जहाँ पत्थर चुप है। वे द्वंद्व, दग़ा, बदलते यार‑दुश्मन और एकल मुकाबलों की कड़ी गिनते हैं जो जंग का रुख मोड़ते हैं। पर इन पर इतिहासकार बहुत सँभलकर चलते हैं।

panels.shot: tight close-up on Alha’s face, one eye shadowed, as he looks past the viewer toward Mahoba
panels.action: Alha’s weathered face fills the frame, sweat and dust on his brow, jaw clenched as if hearing distant cries from within Mahoba; the blurred outline of the fort’s gate is visible behind him.

dialogue.speaker: Alha
dialogue.text: If Mahoba falls, what remains of us but names in the dust?

i18n.hi: अगर महोबा टूटा, तो धूल में हमारे हिस्से में क्या बचेगा सिवा नामों के?

panels.shot: cut to an inscription stone in a field, extreme close-up on engraved Nagari characters catching the light
panels.action: A weathered stone slab lies upright in a quiet field, its Nagari letters carved deep but worn; sunlight strikes the grooves, picking out a name that hints at Prithviraj’s presence in these lands.

dialogue.text: The Madanpur stone speaks more plainly than song. It records Prithviraj III’s campaign into Chandela country and boasts of victory. Through such carvings we know the raid was real.

i18n.hi: मदनपुर का पत्थर गीत से साफ बोलता है। वह पृथ्वीराज तृतीय की चंदेल देश पर चढ़ाई दर्ज करता है और फतह पर इतराता है। इन्हीं नक्काशियों से हमें पता चलता है कि धावा सचमुच पड़ा था।

panels.shot: wide, slightly elevated shot of Mahoba’s streets in turmoil, with gates broken and smoke rising, but no explicit violence
panels.action: A breached gate stands ajar as armoured riders move inside Mahoba; townsfolk flee down a narrow street, smoke curls above rooftops, and temple towers loom in the hazy background.

dialogue.text: Modern scholars, reading these and related records, agree: around 1182–83, Mahoba was taken in a Chauhan assault. The city was sacked, and Paramardi suffered a hard military defeat.

i18n.hi: इन और ऐसे ही साक्ष्यों को पढ़कर आधुनिक विद्वान मानते हैं: 1182–83 के आसपास महोबा चौहान हमले में गिरा। शहर उजड़ गया और परमार्दि को कड़ी सैन्य शिकस्त झेलनी पड़ी।

panels.shot: somber mid-shot of a temple courtyard after the sack, with statues toppled and doors hanging open, a few survivors standing in shock
panels.action: Within a temple courtyard, a stone image lies tipped on its side, offerings scattered; a few weary citizens stand stunned under the open sky, while the distant silhouettes of departing warriors fade beyond the walls.

dialogue.text: The ballads remember this wound with a cry that echoes down the centuries. They dwell not on dates, but on the feel of loss—the sense that a proud centre of power had been humbled.

i18n.hi: किस्से इस घाव को ऐसी चीख में सँभालते हैं जो सदियों तक गूँजती है। वे तारीख़ नहीं, उस खोने की टीस पकड़ते हैं—यह अहसास कि शान से भरा सत्ता‑केंद्र झुका दिया गया।

panels.shot: intimate courtyard scene again with the bard, now leaning forward as listeners hold their breath
panels.action: The bard from earlier leans in, eyes bright with tears, while his listeners watch, faces tense and absorbed, as if living the sack of Mahoba through his words.

dialogue.text: So the Alha songs press onward. Alha fights on; Udal’s death, in some recensions, breaks the king’s heart. And Parmal, overwhelmed by shame at defeat, is said to lay down his life.

i18n.hi: तो अल्हा के गीत आगे बढ़ते जाते हैं। अल्हा लड़ता रहता है; कुछ क़िस्सों में ऊदल की मौत से राजा का कलेजा फट जाता है। और परमार, हार की शर्म से दबा, अपना जीवन त्याग देता कहा जाता है।

panels.shot: sharp cut to a royal inscription being chiseled, with a craftsman mid-strike and a dignified figure overseeing
panels.action: A stonecutter strikes his chisel against a fresh slab as a royal official in simple but rich robes watches; the partly carved inscription includes the name of Paramardi with a later date clearly indicated.

dialogue.text: But other stones refuse this ending. Inscriptions issued in Paramardi’s name continue beyond the raid, reaching into 1201. The king lives, rules, negotiates, and loses again only years later.

i18n.hi: पर कुछ पत्थर इस अंत को नकार देते हैं। परमार्दि के नाम से निकले शिलालेख धावे के बाद भी चलते हैं, 1201 तक पहुँचते हैं। राजा जीता है, राज करता है, सुलह‑सफ़ाई करता है और सालों बाद फिर हार झेलता है।

panels.shot: medium shot of Paramardi seated in a smaller court after Mahoba, expression thoughtful, attendants fewer, backdrop modest
panels.action: Paramardi sits in a humbler audience hall than before, attendants reduced, banners muted; his shoulders sag slightly, but he still listens to a petitioning noble with tired, steady attention.

dialogue.text: Defeat shrinks his power, but does not erase him. From other seats and strongholds, Paramardi tries to hold what remains, as new pressures build from the Ghorid-led armies to the north.

i18n.hi: हार उसकी ताक़त घटाती है, मिटाती नहीं। दूसरी गद्दियों और गढ़ों से परमार्दि जो बचा है, उसे थामे है, जबकि उत्तर से ग़ूरी सेना की नई चढ़ाइयों का दबाव बढ़ता जाता है।

panels.shot: brooding long shot of Kalinjar fort rising on its hill against a stormy sky, small figures of soldiers moving along its walls
panels.action: The massive ridge-top fort of Kalinjar rises under a gathering storm; tiny soldiers patrol its walls while distant clouds darken, hinting at future sieges and changes yet to come.

dialogue.text: Only later, under different attackers, does Kalinjar fall again. Persian chronicler Hasan Nizami describes its storming and the spoils taken, including damage to temples, in the long story of the region’s decline.

i18n.hi: बाद में, और हमलावरों के ज़ोर पर कालिंजर फिर गिरता है। फ़ारसी इतिहासकार हसन निज़ामी इसके फतह, लूट और मंदिरों पर पड़े वार का ज़िक्र करता है, इस सूबे की ढलती तकदीर के लंबे किस्से में।

panels.shot: intercut panel showing Alha and Udal in bardic glory on one side, and a row of inscriptions on the other, like two halves of a frame
panels.action: On the left half, Alha and Udal stand heroic, swords raised before an idealised Mahoba; on the right, a calm line of stone inscriptions recedes into the background like a quiet archive hall.

dialogue.text: Thus two Mahobas stand before us. One is sung, where Alha and Udal’s courage shapes every choice and the king dies of shame. The other is carved, where a defeated Paramardi lives on after the sack.

i18n.hi: यूँ हमारे सामने दो महोबा खड़े हैं। एक गाया जाता है, जहाँ अल्हा‑ऊदल की बहादुरी हर फ़ैसला तय करती है और राजा शर्म से मर जाता है। दूसरा पत्थर में उकेरा है, जहाँ हारा हुआ परमार्दि लूट के बाद भी जिंदा रहता है।

panels.shot: close-up of the bard’s hand resting on a manuscript leaf, with marginal notes and an inscription rubbing beside it
panels.action: A weathered hand presses down a palm-leaf manuscript of the Alha-Khand, while beside it lies a rubbing of an inscription on paper; both rest on the same wooden desk under lamplight.

dialogue.text: Modern scholars like Dikshit and Grierson lay ballad beside stone. They honour the songs as memories of grief and pride, yet gently separate their poetic truth from the firmer dates of inscriptions.

i18n.hi: आधुनिक विद्वान जैसे दीक्षित और ग्रियर्सन गीत को पत्थर के साथ रखकर पढ़ते हैं। वे इन काव्य‑कथाओं को गर्व और ग़म की याद मानकर सम्मान देते हैं, पर उनके काव्यसत्य को शिलालेख की पक्की तारीख़ों से धीरे से अलग कर देते हैं।

panels.shot: poetic mid-shot of Alha standing in a contemporary Bundelkhand landscape, half-real, half-ghost, with farmers and a radio in the background
panels.action: Alha’s semi-transparent figure stands on a rocky Bundelkhand field; behind him farmers work and a small radio rests on a stone, as if his presence is woven into today’s land and sound.

dialogue.text: Yet the songs will not fade. In Bundelkhand, Alha’s verses still roll over loudspeakers, at fairs and fields, carrying the ache of Mahoba’s fall long after its fort and temples turned to quiet stone.

i18n.hi: फिर भी ये गीत मिटते नहीं। बुंदेलखंड में अल्हा की पंक्तियाँ आज भी मेले‑ठेलों और खेतों में लाउडस्पीकरों से गूँजती हैं, महोबा के गिरने का दर्द ढोती हुई, बहुत बाद तक जब उसका क़िला और मंदिर पत्थर की ख़ामोशी बन चुके।

panels.shot: final contemplative wide shot of inscription stones and a distant village, with Alha and Udal’s silhouettes faint against the sky
panels.action: In the foreground, a cluster of old inscription stones stand under a village tree; far beyond, the faint silhouettes of Alha and Udal stride across the horizon, merging with clouds at sunset.

dialogue.text: Between Alha’s song and Paramardi’s stone, we glimpse how people remember defeat: not only through dates and names, but through stories that bend facts to hold on to the hurt that facts alone cannot carry.

i18n.hi: अल्हा के गीत और परमार्दि के पत्थर के बीच हम देखते हैं लोग हार को कैसे याद रखते हैं: सिर्फ़ तारीख़ों और नामों से नहीं, बल्कि ऐसी कहानियों से जो सच को मोड़कर भी उस टीस को थाम लेती हैं जो महज़ तथ्य नहीं उठा पाते।

title_i18n.en: Alha and Udal Between Ballad and Stone
title_i18n.hi: अल्हा‑ऊदल: क़िस्सा और पत्थर के बीच

subtitle_i18n.hi: जब गीत ने पत्थर को ललकारा
